background: Societe Generale is one of France's three largest banks, a universal bank with French retail networks, a large derivatives-driven investment bank, the Ayvens car-leasing business and banking subsidiaries in Africa and Central Europe.
synthesis: All three agencies rate the bank, A+ on average and the weakest of them at A, one on positive, one on stable and one on negative outlook, after a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. The ratios do not flatter it against EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 13.2% and leverage of 4.3% are both in the bottom quarter, LCR of 146% is below the median and NSFR of 115% also in the bottom quarter. Nothing has moved materially over the past four periods, on figures to 30 Jun 2026, so the gap to peers is settled rather than widening, and the ratings have been travelling the other way. Both items flagged in the last 90 days are favourable, a raised profitability target reported on 21 Sep 2026 and an outlook change before it.
